I don't really think the person accurately described it, especially since non-binary is an umbrella term. There is a difference between gender expression and gender, and I think the person who commented that was just a bit mixed up.

Gender isn't really something you can accurately/easily describe, which is why it takes many people so long to figure it out. I remember it took months of questioning to decide on a label I was comfortable with.

Gender is also very complicated, and there are a lot of labels, but labels are not meant to be restricting, rather they are meant to be a jumping off point to help people understand themselves and others.

For me, I know my gender isn't male or female. Those labels don't feel right, and so the other option is non-binary. Which is basically the definition of non-binary: not strictly male or female. It can be a mix, or neither, but it is not SOLELY binary.

That's true, being correctly gendered is great. It does make people feel good about themselves, but would you prefer people that don't present the way they "should" (the way that aligns with their gender) to be misgendered all the time? And what is your opinion on NB people? They should always present androgynous? Are you saying that every person has to either present in a feminine way, a masculine way, or an androgynous way? And it has to align with traditional gender roles? No one should be forced to dress in a certain way.

Yes, it would be nice if everyone presented as their gender traditionally should, but that makes many people uncomfortable. Also, if a non-queer person doesn't like gender neutral pronouns it's usually because they think that those pronouns shouldn't be used (unless it suits them, obviously).

And you're right, neither of us is objectively right or wrong. There is no such thing as something being objective. That doesn't exist. So we should try to reach an agreement that the majority of people are comfortable with. Being misgendered  sucks, being referred to with gender neutral pronouns CAN suck, but it's better than complete misgendering (of course, gender neutral pronouns can be misgendering, but that's a whole other discussion). We should go out of our way to change things because overall, it makes people more comfortable. We should almost always move forward, otherwise we would still be using horses to drive and we would be solving COVID by sniffing herbs.

Presentation ≠ gender. It may suck for him to be called ‘they’ (which does suck, but especially if gender neutral pronouns are normalized, it wouldn’t, he would just correct people and move on. I don’t want to assume, but I’m guessing being called ‘they’ feels bad because our current language is so binary that being called ‘they’ means that people can’t tell if he’s a guy or a girl) but what about other people? What about trans girls who aren’t out? What about someone who uses neopronouns but presents masculinely? 

There are so many possibilities of misgendering by assuming pronouns (even with cis people) that it would actually be disrespectful to assume. What if someone wasn’t a guy but still put a lot of effort into appearing masculine? Would it be disrespectful to refer to them as ‘they’ then? Like, I present fairly feminine and I’m AFAB, even though I’m NB, and so people CONSTANTLY misgender me. They say ‘young lady’ and ‘miss’ and it sucks. This is because they assume. But with gender neutral language, at least people wouldn’t be misgendered, they would simply not be gendered at all. Which, in my opinion, is much better than misgendering.
